conflict_sweep.query: countries_tags:"en:united-states" AND labels_tags:"en:no-gluten" AND (allergens_tags:"en:gluten" OR ingredients_tags:("en:wheat" OR "en:barley" OR "en:rye" OR "en:malt" OR "en:barley-malt" OR "en:malt-extract" OR "en:barley-malt-extract" OR "en:spelt" OR "en:durum-wheat" OR "en:durum-wheat-semolina" OR "en:semolina" OR "en:wheat-flour" OR "en:wheat-starch" OR "en:triticale" OR "en:soy-sauce" OR "en:brewer-s-yeast" OR "en:malt-vinegar" OR "en:barley-malt-syrup" OR "en:gluten" OR "en:wheat-gluten" OR "en:barley-flour" OR "en:rye-flour" OR "en:malted-barley-flour"))

killer_stats.text: Open Food Facts tags 35,876 US products gluten-free. Of the 266 that also carry a gluten-grain ingredient tag and have English ingredient text, 80 still list wheat, barley, rye, malt, or another gluten source once the actual ingredient text is read and qualifiers like 'gluten-free oats' are handled.
killer_stats.frame: OFF conflict sweep: US/Canada barcodes, gluten-free tag, gluten-grain ingredient tag, English ingredient text. A floor for the whole catalog, since untagged products were out of reach.

killer_stats.text: 21 of those 80 conflicting products contain barley or malt, which the FDA allergen 'Contains' statement does not have to mention because barley is not one of the nine major allergens.

Another 253 US products tagged gluten-free carry a gluten allergen tag in Open Food Facts with no gluten-grain ingredient tag; 196 of those 253 contain oats, so a filter built on the allergen tag alone would hide products that are probably fine.
killer_stats.frame: OFF conflict sweep, allergen-tag-only rows (classified from tags; ingredient text was not read)

killer_stats.text: Only 42 of 249 products in this sample with a gluten-free claim could be matched by UPC to GFCO's certified product list; GFCO was the only registry checked, so the rest have no registry confirmation in this pipeline yet.
47 of 57 gluten-free-claimed products that contain oats never say the oats are gluten-free in the ingredient text.
